title: Best Microwave Under Rs 20,000 in India (2026): Convection, Grill & Solo Picks
description: We ranked 7 microwaves under Rs 20,000 in India for convection cooking, grill performance and inverter efficiency. LG, IFB, Samsung, Panasonic compared.
short_desc: LG, IFB, Samsung, Panasonic tested for Indian cooking.

headings.text: What actually matters in a microwave under Rs 20,000
Solo vs grill vs convection: pick by cooking style

cta.headline: Microwave that actually bakes and grills?
cta.sub: A sub-Rs 20,000 convection microwave with a fan-forced heater, grill rack, and 30+ auto-cook menus handles 80 percent of Indian kitchen tasks. We ranked 7 models on heating uniformity, grill browning, convection bake performance, and inverter efficiency.

faq.q: Solo, grill, or convection -- which do I need?
faq.a: Solo microwaves only heat (reheat, defrost, basic cooking). Grill microwaves add a heating element for tandoori, kebabs, and toast. Convection microwaves add a fan-forced heater for baking cakes, pizzas, and roasting. For Indian kitchens, convection is the right pick if you bake even once a month; grill is fine if you only do tandoori; solo is enough if you only reheat and make Maggi. The picks below are all convection.

faq.q: What capacity do I need for an Indian family?
faq.a: 20-23L for bachelors and couples. 25-28L for a family of 3-4. 30L+ for a joint family or if you bake large cakes. Indian thalis fit comfortably up to 28L. Most convection microwaves under Rs 20,000 come in 23-28L, which is the sweet spot.

faq.q: Is inverter microwave worth the premium?
faq.a: Yes if you cook 2+ hours daily. Inverter microwaves deliver consistent power at low settings (instead of cycling full-power on/off like conventional microwaves). This is critical for melting chocolate, softening butter, and slow-cooking dal. The premium is Rs 1,500-3,000 over non-inverter and the cooking quality difference is obvious.

8-12 years for the magnetron (the heating element) with normal use. The control boards and turntable motors last 5-8 years. LG, IFB, Samsung, and Panasonic all have authorised service centres in 200+ Indian cities. Buy from a brand with a service centre in your city -- a microwave that cannot be repaired is a Rs 15,000 paperweight in year 8.

faq.q: Can a convection microwave replace an OTG?
faq.a: For most Indian home baking, yes. A convection microwave + grill rack + 30L capacity handles cakes, cookies, pizzas, and grilled vegetables. An OTG (oven-toaster-griller) is better for toast, croissants, and high-heat roasting (above 220 degrees). If you bake 2-3 times a week, a convection microwave is enough; if you bake daily or run a home bakery, an OTG or built-in oven is better.

tldr_pick: Our top pick is the IFB 30BC4 30L Convection Microwave (Black). 30L capacity (largest in this price range), 101 auto-cook menus, convection + grill + microwave combined, child-lock, and steam clean. IFB service network is the widest in India for kitchen appliances, with 250+ authorised centres. Rs 16,490 on Amazon during sale weeks.
key_takeaways: Convection is non-negotiable for Indian kitchens -- solo microwaves cannot bake or roast.
25-28L is the sweet spot -- fits Indian thalis, large enough for family cooking.
Inverter tech matters for low-power cooking -- melting chocolate, slow-cooking dal.
Auto-cook menus save 5-10 minutes per dish -- 30+ Indian menu options beat 10 generic ones.
who_for: Indian families looking for an all-in-one microwave that heats, grills, and bakes without a separate OTG. Covers bachelors in 1BHK kitchens, couples, and families of 3-4 who cook Indian food daily and want a microwave that also handles baking on weekends.
methodology: We compared 7 popular convection microwaves under Rs 20,000 sold on Amazon India, Flipkart, and brand stores in August 2026. For each, we evaluated capacity, convection wattage, grill wattage, inverter vs non-inverter, auto-cook menu count (Indian vs generic), turntable size, child lock, steam clean, noise in dB, and warranty. Cross-referenced with Indian home-cook reviews and YouTube baking tests.
